exposure: age on admission less than 24 hours
corrected gestational age on admission less than 37 weeks
weight on admission less than 2.5 kg
cohort: Neonates admitted to the premature baby unit of a secondary care hospital in Nawalapitiya, Sri Lanka.
finding: Nearly two out of five neonates admitted to the PBU were hypothermic, and hypothermia on admission was significantly associated with several maternal and neonatal factors, indicating serious neonatal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Lower-segment caesarean sections had a statistically significant association with hypothermia on bivariate analysis.
cross-section timing: Data collected retrospectively from medical records for admissions between April 1, 2021, and March 31, 2022.
birth_weight: Includes neonates with normal birth weight (majority, 52.5%), low birth weight, and those with a weight on admission less than 2.5 kg.
gest_age: Includes term (59%) and premature neonates, with corrected gestational age on admission less than 37 weeks identified as an associated factor.
